key_insight: A workflow-integrated large language model system can automate daily clinical summaries and trial matching in radiation oncology, with early user feedback suggesting strong satisfaction and routine adoption.
clinical_relevance: This approach may reduce clinician time spent on chart review and help surface potentially relevant clinical trials during standard care workflows.
method: Cross-sectional anonymous clinician survey after 1 month of deployment
Daily automated physician-specific email summaries generated by RadOnc-GPT
Included patient schedules, EHR-derived status summaries, and trial identification for new/consult visits
evidence_signal: In 55 respondents, most used the tool daily or several times per week, satisfaction and usability were moderate-to-high, and overall Cronbach’s alpha was 0.97, indicating excellent internal consistency.
watch_item: Findings are based on early self-reported survey data from a single deployed workflow, so real-world time savings and downstream clinical impact remain unproven.
paper_title: The Daily Dose: Workflow-Integrated Large Language Model Automation for Clinical Summarization and Trial Identification in Radiation Oncology
